children: The smart-ring maker Oura is making its way to the public markets, backed by impressive financial growth.

Oura said Thursday night that it had filed its S-1 paperwork with the Securities and Exchange Commission related to its proposed initial public offering. The company plans to be traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "OURA," but didn't specify the size or timing of the offering.
The Wall Street Journal reported in August that Oura planned to go public either this month or next, citing people familiar with the matter. The company declined to provide additional details Friday.

In October 2025, Oura said it had raised more than $900 million in funding, which valued the business at about $11 billion. The company's initial public offering will likely give it a much higher valuation than that. Barron's has reported how rare that is: Out of more than 31,000 VC-funded consumer tech companies, just 0.4% have generated a $1 billion-plus exit, according to PitchBook.

Oura's financials back its funding case. According to the S-1, revenue was $1.21 billion during the nine months ended June 30, 2026, a 74% jump from the prior year period. Net income for those nine months was $60.8 million, surging ahead of the $1.6 million from a year ago.

The business continues to add new customers. Oura sold 1 million rings in the three months ended June 30, up from the 600,000 the year before. The company now has 5 million paid members, who pay a subscription fee to have access to all of Oura's health tracking offerings. This is important for the business, as membership gross margins were 89% for the nine months ended June 30.

Oura started in Finland in 2013 by a group of tech founders that wanted to step into the personal health and wellness space with a wearable device. This device ended up being a ring, with the first version launching in 2015.

Oura rings are now seemingly everywhere. Just look around when commuting on the subway or exercising at the local gym and you'll see people wearing different variations of the rings that come in multiple colors. These devices are meant to provide insights on a person's sleep, activity levels, vitals, menstrual cycles, and more.
